issue_context.title: Panic with `repeat_by` and Date/Datetime datatype
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
from datetime import date
df = pl.DataFrame({
    "repeat": [2,2,2],
    "date": [date(2021,1,1)]*3
})
df.select(pl.col('date').repeat_by('repeat'))

thread '<unnamed>' panicked at /home/runner/work/polars/polars/crates/polars-arrow/src/array/list/mod.rs:82:61:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ComputeError(ErrString("ListArray's child's DataType must match. However, the expected DataType is Date32 while it got Int32."))
```


### Log output

_No response_

### Issue description

Repeat_by with a Date32 data type column worked before on Polars 0.18.15, now it throws an exception. It seems as if it casts it to int32 during the repeat_by. I can see it's broken since 0.19.7.

### Expected behavior

```python
import datetime
from polars.testing import assert_frame_equal

df = pl.DataFrame({
    "repeat": [2,2,2],
    "date": [date(2021,1,1)]*3
})
result = df.select(pl.col('date').repeat_by('repeat'), 'repeat',)

expected = pl.DataFrame(
    [
        pl.Series("date", [[datetime.date(2021, 1, 1), datetime.date(2021, 1, 1)], [datetime.date(2021, 1, 1), datetime.date(2021, 1, 1)], [datetime.date(2021, 1, 1), datetime.date(2021, 1, 1)]], dtype=pl.List(pl.Date)),
        pl.Series("repeat", [2, 2, 2], dtype=pl.Int64),
    ]
)
assert_frame_equal(result,expected)
```

```
shape: (3, 2)
┌──────────────────────────┬────────┐
│ date                     ┆ repeat │
│ ---                      ┆ ---    │
│ list[date]               ┆ i64    │
╞══════════════════════════╪════════╡
│ [2021-01-01, 2021-01-01] ┆ 2      │
│ [2021-01-01, 2021-01-01] ┆ 2      │
│ [2021-01-01, 2021-01-01] ┆ 2      │
└──────────────────────────┴────────┘
```

comments: My temp workaround is to cast Date to int64 first and then after repeat_by cast it back to Date, but this not ideal of course. :)
Thanks for reporting this, will take a look right now.
Thanks @reswqa, I have the exact same issue on polars 0.19.9.

review_comments: This `inner_dtype` seems should be the dtype of backed `values` instead of `out(maybe logical)`.
